notes: Open by stressing that sequencing is the control mechanism: Gujarat should not scale every intervention at once. Point to Horizon 1 as the evidence gate, Horizon 2 as the replication engine, and Horizon 3 as the institutional handoff. Expect a question on district selection; answer with water stress, value density, and delivery readiness.
title: A **3-horizon** roadmap moves Gujarat from proof of value to statewide adoption by sequencing delivery, infrastructure, and policy adoption
subtitle: The execution logic is to validate district-specific interventions first, then scale through clusters and institutions so water-smart gains and value-chain upgrades stick without overwhelming frontline systems.

phases.title: Horizon 1 proves the operating model in lead districts before statewide budgets and systems are committed
phases.body: Start where the case is strongest: water-stressed horticulture belts, dairy-linked zones, and high-gap smallholder systems. Test a tight package that combines micro-irrigation activation, crop advisories, aggregation support, and post-harvest fixes, then track farmer uptake, service reliability, and margin improvement by production system rather than by scheme.

phases.title: Horizon 2 scales through district clusters so execution expands only where capabilities and market linkages are already workable
phases.body: Replicate only the models that hold under real field conditions, using cluster expansion across districts with similar water profiles, crop economics, and buyer access. Add the missing enablers in sequence—nurseries, FPO operations, chilling or grading, and input-service partnerships—so adoption rises with market pull instead of outrunning delivery capacity.

phases.title: Horizon 3 embeds successful models into statewide systems so adoption continues after the initial program push
phases.body: Convert the best-performing packages into routine state and partner delivery through extension workflows, data dashboards, financing channels, and commodity-specific procurement linkages. The end-state is not a larger pilot; it is a repeatable execution architecture that lets districts choose the right package while the state standardizes monitoring, incentives, and resilience metrics.
